hero_line: A Portland songwriter since 2022, Amos Heart played Pickathon close to home, then shared a Laurelthirst residency with The Apricots.
Years into Appalachian gothic country, Angela Autumn played Pickathon in 2025, then released Believer on Gar Hole and toured Europe.
The Australian-born bassist behind Mighty Vertebrate played Pickathon in 2025, then toured with Flea and released Beginningless.
Austin's Being Dead came to Pickathon off EELS, a record on three best-of-2024 lists, then headlined across the UK and Europe.
A New York guitarist since 2012, Ben Seretan played Pickathon the year Youth Pastoral was reissued, then released Sunbeam of No Illusion.
Blu & Exile built on Below the Heavens for two decades, played Pickathon in 2025, then took Time Heals Everything on a world tour.
The New Orleans songwriter behind Famous Lunch played Pickathon in 2025, then released a new single and set out on a fall duo tour.
Virginia bluegrass and country about working lives: Colby T. Helms played Pickathon in 2025, then followed with One For The Losers.
The Wand frontman returned to Pickathon under his own name, a week after I Love People, then took the solo songs to Europe.
Omaha's David Nance came back to Pickathon on a bill with Rosali, then went out on his first solo acoustic tour in over a decade.
A bağlama player from Hamburg, Derya Yıldırım brought Anatolian psych-rock to Pickathon behind Yarın Yoksa, then toured Europe.
Weeks after the live album At Tubby's, Dougie Poole played Pickathon with his band, then toured North America with Jake Xerxes Fussell.
The Los Angeles band behind Free Energy played Pickathon in 2025, moved to Polyvinyl, and released do you love the color of the sky?
From a seven-year bar residency to the IBMA's New Artist award, East Nash Grass played Pickathon, then won the IBMA's Album of the Year.
Austin honky-tonk with a band of the city's veterans: Ellis Bullard returned to Pickathon a year after his first visit and kept touring.
Nashville honky-tonk singer Emily Nenni returned to Pickathon two years after her first visit, then released Movin' Shoes on New West.
Kahil El'Zabar founded the Ethnic Heritage Ensemble in 1973. Fifty-two years in, they played Pickathon, then toured behind Skydancer.
A Portland post-punk band since 2013, Forty Feet Tall made their Pickathon debut, then released Clean the Cage at a hometown show.
From Bogotá, Mario Galeano Toro's band has recorded for Soundway and Vampisoul; in 2025 they played Pickathon and toured the U.S.
Eric D. Johnson started Fruit Bats in 1997, then found a second voice in Bonny Light Horseman. In 2025 he wrote Baby Man in ten days.
A Portland indie-folk band Willamette Week named a best new band of 2022, Glitterfox played Pickathon, then released decoder.
Two decades on the festival circuit led Greensky Bluegrass to open Pickathon's Thursday, then headline Red Rocks with Margo Price.
From café stages to an NPR Tiny Desk, Haley Heynderickx returned to Pickathon for a third time, then released What of Our Nature.
Hannah Cohen played Pickathon months after Earthstar Mountain came out, then watched it reach year-end lists and opened for Caamp.
Minneapolis songwriter Siri Undlin played Pickathon after recording Right On live to tape, then released Morning When It Comes.
Psych-pop harmonies and dry jokes from Atlanta: Improvement Movement played Pickathon, then released Your Perfect Real Life on ATO.
Tacoma's Justin R. Cruz Gallego followed his Sub Pop debut with a Pickathon visit in 2025, then toured clubs across the U.S. and Canada.
A fiddler and banjo player tracing Black and Indigenous string-band roots, Jake Blount played Pickathon, then released Single-Footing Horse.
The summer he won the Traditional Roots Album Juno, Saskatchewan's Jake Vaadeland played Pickathon, then signed with Dine Alone Records.
Portland outlaw country band Jenny Don't And The Spurs played Pickathon, then released Live at the Jenny and toured Europe.

act: Jimetta Rose & The Voices of Creation
hero_line: Jimetta Rose leads a Los Angeles choir of gospel and soul that played North Sea Jazz, then Pickathon, then announced MettaSun.
Only a few months into life as a Portland band, Jonny's Day Out played Pickathon in 2025 and returned the next year.
The saxophonist and producer behind The Omnichord Real Book played Pickathon in 2025, then released Animative with Meshell Ndegeocello.
Singing in Cajun French with Les Rôdailleurs, Jourdan Thibodeaux played Pickathon, then Maui and Quebec, and helped start French classes.
After moving from Portland to New Orleans, Kassi Valazza wrote From Newman Street about leaving, toured Europe and returned to Pickathon.
Laney Jones took her band The Spirits on their first national headline tour in 2025, with Pickathon as one stop, then released their debut.
Vermont indie rock, loud and quiet: Lily Seabird played Pickathon after Trash Mountain, then released Lightspheres On Their Way.
Lonesome Shack has played hypnotic country blues since 2006, recorded In Montargis in a hotel in France, then played Pickathon.
From Victoria, B.C., Ocie Elliott went platinum in Canada, opened for Zach Bryan at Red Rocks, then returned to Pickathon in 2025.
Olive Klug writes plainspoken folk; their second album, Lost Dog, arrived on Signature Sounds, and they played Pickathon that summer.
Alaska's Portugal. The Man won a Grammy for Feel It Still, played Pickathon in 2025, then released Shish and went on tour.
Atlanta duo Revival Season played Green Man behind their debut, Golden Age Of Self Snitching, then Pickathon, then a second record.
Fabi Reyna's Reyna Tropical won a Libera Award for Malegría, played Pickathon, then released Helado Tropical with Helado Negro.
Rosali plays in David Nance's band and records for Merge; she came back to Pickathon with Nance, then released Slow Pain.
Ripley Johnson's country-psych project Rose City Band followed Sol y Sombra with Pickathon, between festival dates and a fall tour.
A Portland country-punk songwriter since 2024, Rose Gerber played Pickathon, then began a monthly protest-song night at The Showdown.
SML grew out of four nights of improvising in a Los Angeles jazz bar, then played Pickathon, Newport Jazz and North Sea Jazz.
Daniel Donato's keys player and singer brought gospel roots to Pickathon under his own name, then took his songs to clubs.
Melbourne's Surprise Chef plays moody, cinematic funk; Superb came out in May 2025, they played Pickathon, then released Frogs in a Pond.
Six decades into the blues, Taj Mahal played Pickathon in 2025, the year of his Keb' Mo' record, then earned a Grammy nomination.
Brothers Jack Torrey and Page Burkum came back to Pickathon thirteen years after their first, having recorded with Dan Auerbach.
Led by Big Chief Joseph Boudreaux Jr., The Rumble played Pickathon after two Grammy nominations, then released Ain't No Dying.
A young Chicano soul group from California, Thee Heart Tones played Pickathon with labelmates Thee Marloes, then shared a Los Angeles bill.
The soul trio from Surabaya, Indonesia, played Pickathon behind Perak, then released Di Hotel Malibu and shared a Los Angeles bill.
John Ross's heartland-leaning Wild Pink played Pickathon after Dulling the Horns made Paste's top ten, then released Still Coming Down.
